main_text.p: regionem ducere non possent, sed ut ne singuli quidem hostem effugerent, qui transfire conarentur. Hæc Amilcar videns, &c. Idem Polybius libro eodem belli hujus ejusdem causas & initia exponens de Tunete oppido Carthagini vicino sic ait: Mercenarii irâ succensi adversus Carthaginienses, infesti adurbem feruntur; & quindecim millia passuum abeâ Tunete castra ponunt. Erant bi supra viginti millia. Tum demum Carthaginiensibus error suus ob oculos obversari, cum nihil eos sera pœnitentia juvabat. Et post pauca memorat, Gesconem ducem ad placandos eosdem hos iratos milites cum pecuniâ ex urbe Carthagine missum, profectumque mari Tunetem appulisse: ubi verba Græca cum aliis sic habent: Ὁ Γέσκων [illegible, ~12 letters] μάτων, [?] εἰς τ[?] Τύ- νητα, τὸ μὲν ἀπο[?] [?]ν λαμβάνειν τὰς ἡγεμόνας, &c. Quæ verba significare videntur, per mare navigari potuisse & appelli Tunetem. Iudicium lectori relinquo. Et rursum idem libro xiv. Tunes Carthagine abest stadia quasi cxx. page.notes: The Greek passage is only partly legible from the scan. Its letters are given where they could be seen. Where a stretch could not be read, it is marked as illegible, and the other doubtful letters carry [?]. The italic and roman boundaries are read from the scan and may be slightly off. The final word "quique" is printed with a Greek-looking "e" in its second half; it is probably a Latin "e" (quique), and I have left it as read with the doubtful letter marked. The catchword "con-" sits at the foot of the page, not in the body text.
